phase.BASE: You're building your base and habit now — volume rises, intensity stays low.
phase.BUILD: Build phase: we add quality on top of the base and keep growth under control.
phase.PEAK: Peak of preparation: the hardest work, fatigue is expected and allowed.
phase.TAPER: Taper: volume drops so you arrive at the start fresh.
phase.RACE: Everything this week serves the race — the day that paid for all the work.

effortSuffix.TAPER: Stay at the lower end of the range.

EASY.why: Easy running builds your aerobic base and helps you recover between hard sessions — slow is deliberate.
how: Keep a conversational pace for the whole run.
If you speed up, ease back: the ceiling is a speed, not a target.
EASY.mistake: An "easy" day at a moderate pace (RPE 6) — then no day is truly easy or hard.
EASY.effortCue: you can talk in full sentences without losing your breath.

LONG.why: It builds endurance, efficiency and mental toughness for the closing stages of a race.
LONG.whyWithDistance: Long run {{km, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} km — builds endurance, efficiency and mental toughness for the closing stages of a race.
how: Start calmly, the first 5 km the slowest.
Hydrate and test your kit the way you will on race day.
LONG.mistake: Starting too fast drains you before the end — the long run should give you confidence, not break you.
LONG.effortCue: you talk in sentences and breathe under control.

TEMPO.why: Tempo work raises your lactate threshold — a pace you can hold for ~1 h becomes easier over time.
how: Warm up 2 km, then hold the tempo block evenly, without surges.
If you can only speak in single words, you've gone too far.
TEMPO.mistake: Tempo at 5 km pace isn't tempo — it becomes a VO2max session and demands too much recovery.
TEMPO.effortCue: comfortably hard, you speak in short phrases.

INTERVALS.why: Intervals raise your VO2max — the ceiling of aerobic power and the speed you can sustain.
how: Keep the first 1–2 reps calmer, make the last as strong as the first.
Recovery: easy jog or walk, bring your breathing down.
INTERVALS.mistake: Going out too hard → pointless fatigue instead of a productive stimulus; reps get slower and slower.
INTERVALS.effortCue: hard but controlled, technique holds together.

REPETITIONS.why: Reps don't build endurance — they sharpen mechanics, stride and running economy.
how: Every repetition fast and relaxed, without tension.
Full recovery before the next one (walk or easy jog).
REPETITIONS.mistake: R-pace as intervals: without full recovery your mechanics fall apart and there's no speed stimulus.
REPETITIONS.effortCue: short and clean; when technique drops, stop the set.

REST.why: Rest isn't a break from training — adaptation happens while your body recovers.
how: A walk, mobility or light stretching for 15–20 min.
Priority: 7–9 h of sleep and normal eating.
REST.mistake: Filling the day with junk kilometres or feeling guilty — rest is part of the plan.
REST.effortCue: today you don't train, today you're building.

RACE.why: The day the whole plan was made for — a check of form, tactics and head.
how: Run the first half under control, don't chase anyone else's pace.
Stick to your pace plan to the end.
RACE.mistake: A fast start burns your energy — the most common reason for fading in the second half.
RACE.effortCue: hard, but to plan; the last third is allowed to hurt.

STRENGTH.why: Strength stabilises joints and corrects imbalances — fewer injuries and a more efficient stride (+8–12% for 1–2 sessions a week).
how: Controlled form above weight; the last 1–2 reps challenging but clean.
Don't leave heavy leg work for the day before a key run session.
STRENGTH.mistake: Too heavy and too close to quality running — strength then steals recovery instead of supporting it.
STRENGTH.effortCue: you feel the muscles working, form stays clean.

pre.meal: Meal 2–3 h before running: rich in carbs (pasta, oatmeal), a little fat and protein.
pre.snackLong: Snack 2–3 h before: 75+ g carbs + some protein.
pre.snackMedium: Snack 60–90 min before: 50+ g carbs + some protein.
pre.snackShort: Snack before heading out: 25+ g carbs (banana, toast with honey).
pre.water: Drink ~500 ml of water 2 h before the start.
pre.race: Test your gels and timing in training — nothing new on race day.

during.gel: Gel {{index, number}} — drink ~200 ml of water.

post.recovery: Within 1–2 h: protein + carbs (chocolate milk, yoghurt + fruit, a sandwich).
post.rehydrate: Rehydration: ~1.5 L of fluid per kg of lost weight, with sodium.

checklist.kit: Pack your kit: shoes, socks, shorts and shirt (tested in training)
checklist.bib: Pin your race bib to your shirt
checklist.fuel: Prepare gels, electrolytes and a bottle
checklist.logistics: Check the route to the start and bib pickup
checklist.dropBag: Pack a drop bag: dry shirt, snack and shoes for after
checklist.breakfast: Breakfast 2–3 h before the start (tested in training)
checklist.hydrate: Drink 200–300 ml of water 60–90 min before the start
checklist.antichafe: Anti-chafe on thighs, underarms and feet
checklist.warmupLong: Short 10 min warm-up + a few strides
checklist.firstKmLong: First km disciplined — 5–10 s/km slower than goal
checklist.firstKmShort: Controlled and strong from the start, no sprinting
checklist.gelPlan: A gel every 30–35 min + water at every station
checklist.effort: Run by effort through wind and hills, not by the watch
checklist.finishLong: Let it rip in the last 2 km if you have it
checklist.finishShort: Let it rip in the last km

weather.storm: Thunderstorm — check the race rules and stick to your fuelling plan.
weather.rain: Rain — anti-chafe, a cap and dry socks; pace stays the same.
weather.heat: Hot — start more conservatively and drink at every station.
weather.cold: Cold — layers for the start wait and a longer warm-up.
weather.wind: Wind — run by effort, don't chase the watch.
weather.air: Poor air — lower the intensity and monitor how you feel.
